clue.text: Select path US designed for high flyer

indicators.note: something designed is laid out afresh, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American engineer chooses a route for an aircraft or rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges SELECT, PATH and US together.
explanation.definitionFit: A reusable orbiting craft flies higher than almost anything, a playful description of a launch vehicle.

clue.text: Download history describing old Constable

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw round, as in describing a circle, so one piece goes around the others

parts.note: history is the past
DC stands for Detective Constable, a British police rank

explanation.surface: A digital download of a history of the painter John Constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing round. Constable looks like the landscape painter, but it is the police rank of Detective Constable.
explanation.definitionFit: An audio programme fetched to a phone or computer is an example of a file one downloads.

clue.text: Crooks, it's said, are fast runners

indicators.note: it's said tells us to go by how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: crooks are swindlers or cheaters

explanation.surface: A claim that criminals are quick on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word for swindlers sounds the same as the big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: These spotted African cats are the fastest land animals, so they are literally fast runners.

clue.text: Belt commandos hard

parts.note: the SAS (Special Air Service) is the British Army's special forces regiment
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An order telling soldiers to strike forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of cloth worn round the waist is a kind of belt.

clue.text: Thankless international organisation reported place packed with ashes

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so we go by how the phrase sounds

parts.note: a place is a fireplace or grate; packed with ashes it is a grate that is full

explanation.surface: A disgruntled report from a global body about a fireplace choked with ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns 'grate full' into a sound-alike adjective, placed after UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thankless means showing no gratitude, the opposite of appreciative.

clue.text: Discover barristers examining brief

indicators.note: to discover is to uncover, so the letters are found lying within these words

explanation.surface: Uncovering lawyers poring over a legal brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a lawyer's case papers, but it is an adjective meaning short.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief remark is a short, curt one, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Elevated god with appreciation for horror

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised up means read from bottom to top, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
an eye for something is an appreciation of it, as in an eye for beauty

explanation.surface: A lofty deity with good taste confronting something dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' reverses EROS + EYE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hideous to look at, such as an ugly building, can be called a horror.

clue.text: Abandoned writer, shortly looking outside and searching for hidden stream

indicators.note: outside means the first word goes round the other piece

parts.note: looking at something is watching it

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged
shortly means cut short, so the last letter of writer is dropped

explanation.surface: A neglected author peers out while hunting for an underground watercourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims writer before 'Abandoned' scrambles it to TERWI; 'outside' wraps the looking word round that.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowsing with a forked rod to find underground water is also known by this name.

clue.text: Eyes an American woman showing programs overseas

parts.note: to eye is to look carefully at, or study
an means one, giving A
broad is American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone looks over an American woman demonstrating computer software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programs' in the American spelling suggests software, but here it means courses of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses of learning taken in a foreign country are described by this phrase, as in a year spent on them.

clue.text: Commercial before 11 is direct

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, or AD
11 points to the answer at 11 across, an item of clothing; a frock is one such item

explanation.surface: An advert comes ahead of the next clue's item, which is straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct a letter is to write the destination on it, which is the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Singular outfit exhibiting good paintings about guys

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word holds the other

parts.note: paintings are art
guys are men

explanation.surface: A strange get-up displayed at a show of pictures of blokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like 'odd', but it means a single item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: One item of clothing is a single piece of an outfit.

clue.text: What player discarded to be precise

parts.note: discarded means former, given by the prefix used for a former partner
a performer does a turn or routine on stage, an act

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which card a gamesman threw away, put carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a card game, but it is a stage performer whose routine has been dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate in every detail is the sense shared by the two adjectives.

clue.text: Chest insert in doctor's list

parts.note: a chest is a case or box
to insert something, such as a disc or a film, is to load it

explanation.surface: An instruction to slip a chest X-ray into a medical record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' suggests the body in a medical setting, but it is a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's patients make up their workload, the number of people they must see.

clue.text: No charge excluded as barn dances arranged — those in Spain?

indicators.note: excluded tells us these letters are taken out of the mix
arranged means the remaining letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Free country dances, set up in a foreign style, with a question about Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded' takes N and C out of AS BARN DANCES; 'arranged' shuffles what is left. The definition points back to the dances.
explanation.definitionFit: These slow stately dances in triple time originated in Spain, so they are dances of that country.

clue.text: One producing small movements with market, each tip-off activated

indicators.note: activated means set in motion, so the letters are stirred up
tip-off means the tip, or first letter, comes off the word each

explanation.surface: A trader on the market floor acts on an insider's warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-off' leaves ACH; 'activated' shuffles it with the market letters. 'small movements' are the mechanisms of wristwatches.
explanation.definitionFit: The mechanism inside a timepiece is called its movement, and a craftsman who makes small ones fits this description.

clue.text: Fine summer in Nice for festival

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
été is French for summer, and Nice is in France

explanation.surface: Good weather on the Riviera for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective but is the French city, signalling a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A village fair or outdoor celebration is a kind of festival.

clue.text: Able to make story after being this low

parts.words: Able to make story after being this
parts.note: in a down clue, putting the word able underneath par makes parable, a story

explanation.surface: A golfer feeling poorly still manages to tell a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction, the word able set under par, builds a parable; 'low' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling below one's normal level of health is what it means to be low.

clue.text: Check website regularly is on time

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it
regularly means taking every other letter of website

explanation.surface: Routinely inspect whether a site is running on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something out to see if it works is a synonym of the verb in the clue.

clue.text: Enrols in Society to drink, accepting gin cocktail

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone joins a society for the drinking, especially of gin cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes the gin to IGN, and 'accepting' places that within the society-and-drink pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To register for a club or course is to join it, the same as putting one's name down.

clue.text: Large body found at otherwise endless wild party

parts.note: Saturn is a large planet, a heavenly body

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: alias means otherwise known as

explanation.surface: A big figure turns up at a rowdy party under another name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final letter, leaving ALIA. The Roman festival of the planet's namesake god was notorious for revelry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman midwinter festival was famous for revelry, so its name now means any riotous party.

clue.text: Gentlemen's way, having three to be entertained

indicators.note: entertained means received as a guest, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
tri is the prefix meaning three

explanation.surface: A gentlemen's way of life involves hosting three guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gentlemen's' is the sign on a men's toilet, so it stands for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a public toilet for men is labelled the gentlemen's, which matches this word for a toilet.

clue.text: State what old sopranos can't achieve in the main

indicators.note: state means say aloud, so we go by the sound of the phrase

parts.note: ageing sopranos lose their top notes, the high Cs

explanation.surface: A rueful observation about the limits of an ageing singer's voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic usage calls the open ocean the main, as in the Spanish Main, and these are the waters beyond any country's control.

clue.text: What you do alone without Victor

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word surrounds the letter

parts.note: sole means alone, as in the sole survivor
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A remark about what a person does on their own, missing a friend called Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. 'What you do' refers to the solver working out this very clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword solver's job is to work out the clues, so this is what the reader is doing.

clue.text: Record some regret, nervously rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse
some means a part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Write down a few anxious regrets that were turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes RETNE from inside 'regret, nervously'; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To write an item in a log or ledger is to record it.

clue.text: Unarguably embraces upset relative

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards
embraces means the word holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: Without doubt a family member has become distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' finds NARG in Unarguably, and 'upset' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother, given this familiar name, is a family relative.

clue.text: Huddled together about space next to street light

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

explanation.surface: People crowded together around a gap beside a streetlamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses EN, a printer's space, to give NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuggling close together for warmth is to huddle, so the two past forms match.

clue.text: Model I parcel up

indicators.note: up can mean in disorder, as in things being all up in the air, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wraps a scale model in paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like part of 'parcel up', but it rearranges I PARCEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy of an object made to show what it looks like is a model of it.

clue.text: Polite comments about delightful figs, perhaps roughly heard

indicators.note: roughly heard means the phrase only approximately sounds like the answer

parts.note: delightful means pleasant, and figs are an example of trees, shown by perhaps

explanation.surface: Courteous remarks made about some charming fig trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks figs as an example of trees; said quickly the phrase gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small talk exchanged out of courtesy, such as remarks on the weather, is this kind of polite comment.
